walkthroughs.body_html:
Depth Study: China c1930-c1990 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Depth Study: China c1930-c1990 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Depth Study: China c1930-c1990.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many died in the Great Leap Forward famine?
options: 1 million
15-45 million
100 million

mcqs.q: Who led the Cultural Revolution Red Guards?
options: Deng Xiaoping
Mao Zedong
Zhou Enlai
Lin Biao

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.
He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
Huguenots were Catholic refugees fleeing Cromwell.

mcqs.q: Why was Vesalius significant in the history of medicine?
options: His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.
Huguenots were Catholic refugees fleeing Cromwell.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.

mcqs.q: Why did Huguenots migrate to England from the 1680s?
options: Louis XIV's 1685 revocation of the Edict of Nantes ended toleration of French Protestants; many fled persecution to Protestant England, bringing skills like silk weaving.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
Huguenots were Catholic refugees fleeing Cromwell.
Huguenots came to England because France was poorer than England.
